the synthesis and purification of L-(1-1C)-tyrosin is possible with a yield of 2%–5%, that accumulation in experimental tumors and in human neoplastic tissue is possible, and that positron emission tomographic imaging of the tumor protein synthesis rate is feasible.

the development of a new method for measuring the rate of protein turnover in human neoplastic tissue.
the development of a method to measure the rate of tumor protein synthesis in vivo by positron emission computed tomography.
the development of DL-(1- 11C)-tyroisne for the non-invasive measurement of protein synthesis in tumors by positron emission computed tomography.

DL-(1-1C)-tyrosin is a useful probe for the study of tumor metabolism by positrons emission tomography, and that L-(1-1-C) tyrosin is the isomer of choice.
